:::{#def-channel}
#### Discrete memoryless channel

A **discrete channel** has a finite *[input](#def-channel) alphabet* $\mathcal{X}$,
a finite *output alphabet* $\mathcal{Y}$,
and, for each [input](#def-channel) $x \in \mathcal{X}$,
a [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $p(y \mid x)$ on $\mathcal{Y}$:
the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) that the channel outputs $y$ when it is sent $x$.
The channel is **memoryless** if, over $n$ uses,
each output depends only on the input sent at that use:

$$
\P(Y_1 = y_1, \dots, Y_n = y_n \mid X_1 = x_1, \dots, X_n = x_n)
= \prod_{i=1}^{n} p(y_i \mid x_i).
$$

This is the setup of @cover2006elements [chapter 7].

:::
